title: The pet rescue knows your dog
scenario: A local rescue account messages after you post that your dog is missing. They say a volunteer found a matching dog and ask for a small “scanner and transport fee” before sharing the location.

answers.A: Pay the small fee because the rescue account knows your dog’s name and description.
answers.B: Ask for verifiable evidence such as a live video or identifying detail, and contact the rescue through its official published channel before paying.
answers.C: Meet at a safe public location or animal shelter without paying a release fee first.

explanation: Public lost-pet posts give scammers everything needed to sound specific. Verification should involve the animal, not just the post details.
proTip: Information from your post is not secret proof.
